title: BEFORE vs AFTER Triggers & Audit Logging
description: Sanitize data before writing with BEFORE triggers and record audit trails with AFTER triggers.

data.text: **`BEFORE` triggers** execute before row data is written to disk, allowing you to sanitize, normalize, or reject the operation by returning `NEW` or `NULL`. **`AFTER` triggers** run after data has been persisted, making them ideal for audit trails and notification dispatching.

data.title: Automated Audit Logging with AFTER Trigger
data.content: Recording historical changes to customer records.
data.code:
-- 1. Trigger Function
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION log_customer_changes()
RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$
BEGIN
    INSERT INTO customer_audit_log (
        customer_id, 
        operation, 
        changed_by, 
        old_data, 
        new_data
    )
    VALUES (
        COALESCE(NEW.id, OLD.id),
        TG_OP,
        current_user,
        to_jsonb(OLD),
        to_jsonb(NEW)
    );
    RETURN NEW;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

-- 2. Bind AFTER Trigger
CREATE TRIGGER trg_customer_audit
AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON customers
FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION log_customer_changes();

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use `BEFORE` triggers to modify `NEW` columns before writing to disk.
Use `AFTER` triggers for audit tables and foreign key side-effects.
